question: Three separate electrolytic cells receive the same quantity of electrons, 0.20 mol, at their cathodes. The available metal ions are Ag⁺, Cu^, and Pb^, respectively. Which metal mass is greatest?

For silver:

n(Ag)=0.20 mol



m(Ag)=0.20×108
=21.6 g

Cu^{2++2e⁻→ Cu}



n(Cu)=(0.20 / 2)=0.10 mol

For lead:


Pb^{2++2e⁻→ Pb}

title: Inferring electrode material and copper mass from oxygen production
question: A copper sulphate solution is electrolysed using either inert platinum electrodes or active copper electrodes. The anode gas measurement gives 5.6 L of oxygen at STP. Using the specified half-equations, which conclusion is correct?

options.text: The anode must be copper; 31.75 g of copper is deposited because copper dissolves at the anode.
The anode is inert; the oxygen production corresponds to 0.25 mol of O₂, and 31.75 g of copper is deposited at the cathode.
The anode is inert; the oxygen production corresponds to 0.25 mol of O₂, and 63.5 g of copper is deposited at the cathode.
The anode is copper; oxygen is evolved and no copper is deposited at the cathode.

explanation:
First calculate the oxygen quantity:


n(O₂)=(5.6 / 22.4)=0.25 mol


Oxygen is formed at the inert anode according to


4OH⁻→2H_2O+O₂+4e⁻


The electrons released are


n(e⁻)=0.25×4=1.00 mol


At the cathode,


Cu^{2++2e⁻→ Cu}


Therefore,


n(Cu)=(1.00 / 2)=0.50 mol



m(Cu)=0.50×63.5
=31.75 g


The specified active copper anode would dissolve rather than produce oxygen. Option C doubles the mass of copper by overlooking the two electrons required per copper ion.

title: Integrated conceptual question: Electrolysis of aqueous copper sulphate
question: A student electrolyses aqueous copper sulphate using inert platinum electrodes. Copper is deposited at the cathode, oxygen forms at the anode, and the blue colour gradually fades. Which explanation accounts for all three observations?

options.text: Copper ions are oxidised at the cathode, oxygen ions are reduced at the anode, and copper sulphate is converted into sodium sulphate.
Copper metal is deposited at the anode, hydrogen is deposited at the cathode, and the blue colour fades because platinum dissolves.
Copper ions remain unchanged, oxygen comes from the platinum electrodes, and the blue colour fades because the solution evaporates.

The cathode reaction is


Cu^{2++2e⁻→ Cu}


The specified anode reaction is


4OH⁻→2H_2O+O₂+4e⁻


Copper ions are removed from the solution and are not replenished by the inert platinum anode. Consequently, the blue colour gradually fades. Option B incorrectly reverses the electrode products and assumes that platinum dissolves.

title: Conceptual trap: What determines conductivity?
question: Two electrolyte solutions contain the same total number of dissolved particles. Solution P contains many mobile ions, whereas Solution Q contains mostly neutral molecules and relatively few ions. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

Neither solution can conduct because all dissolved particles are surrounded by water.

explanation:

title: Equal mass changes with active copper electrodes
question: During electrolysis of CuSO₄(aq) using copper electrodes, the cathode gains 12.7 g of copper. Assuming the specified electrode reactions proceed with no other mass change, which result is correct?

options.text: The anode loses 6.35 g, and 0.10 mol of copper dissolves.
The anode loses 12.7 g, and 0.20 mol of copper dissolves.
The anode gains 12.7 g, and no copper dissolves.
The anode loses 25.4 g, and 0.40 mol of copper dissolves.

explanation:
The cathode reaction is


Cu^{2++2e⁻→ Cu}


Moles of deposited copper:


n(Cu)=(12.7 / 63.5)=0.20 mol


With active copper electrodes, the anode reaction is


Cu→ Cu^{2++2e⁻}


The same amount of copper dissolves at the anode as is deposited at the cathode. Hence, the anode loses 12.7 g, corresponding to 0.20 mol of copper.

Option A incorrectly halves the required mass change.
